stem:
A child is carried in after a fall from a trampoline onto concrete. There is an obvious open forearm fracture and a lot of blood on the clothes. He is pale and quiet.

What is the first step in assessment and management?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Open-fracture debridement is important and time-sensitive, but it is not the first action in a pale quiet trauma patient.

options.label: B
options.text: Apply a sling to save the nerve
options.explanation: Splinting protects soft tissue and nerves after the primary survey. It is not the opening move.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An obvious fracture is a distracting injury. The first step is a primary survey (airway with C-spine, breathing, circulation with haemorrhage control, disability) to find life threats. Only then come reduction, sling, and orthopaedics.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Reducing the arm first skips airway and bleeding. A quiet pale child may be shocked or obstructing.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Orthopaedics will be needed, but not before ABCD. Life threats outrank the open fracture.

context:
Paediatric trauma: <C>ABCDE / ABCD first, even when a dramatic limb injury is visible.

Catastrophic haemorrhage, airway, breathing, then circulation. Fracture care follows.
